section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the light of Ein Sof encompasses both the highest ascent and the lowest descent, corresponding to Atzilus and BYA, rooted in the two aspects of light and power within Ein Sof.
section.t: And this is the light of Ein Sof, ascending to the highest height without end and descending to the lowest depth without limit,
"above" and "below" refer to Atzilus and BYA,
and the root of their coming into being is from the two aspects of light and power within Ein Sof,
which themselves are also analogous to "above" and "below."
For the aspect of power within Ein Sof is the matter of descent downward,
that it is within the power of Ein Sof to spread forth and descend downward to become in the category of a separate power to bring into being a yesh and a separate entity,
and the aspect of the light within Him
(the awareness that all matters are as naught)
is the matter of ascent upward.
And this is the light of Ein Sof, ascending to the highest height without end and descending to the lowest depth without limit,
that the elevation and perfection of the light of Ein Sof is in these two aspects.
First,
that it is drawn downward to bring into being and vitalize the creations of BYA,
and in this very thing—descending to the lowest depth without limit,
that it is drawn not only into Beriah and Yetzirah but also into Asiyah,
and within Asiyah itself—into this physical world, below which there is no lower.
And second,
that even the highest worlds,
Atzilus and above Atzilus,
ascending to the highest height without end,
are incomparable and as naught relative to Him, blessed is He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates that the concepts of "above" and "below" apply within both Atzilus and BYA, rooted in the absolute incomparability of all worlds relative to the Ein Sof before the tzimtzum, as perceived through the surrounding light.
section.t: And one may add,
that what was stated above, that "above" and "below" are Atzilus and BYA, is in general terms,
but in particular,
the matter of "above" and "below" exists both in Atzilus and in BYA.
For even in Atzilus and above Atzilus there is the aspect of "below,"
and likewise conversely,
that even in BYA there is the aspect of "above."
And the explanation is,
that the true essence of the matter of incomparability
(that all worlds are incomparable relative to Him, blessed is He)
is that Atzilus
(and even above Atzilus)
and Asiyah are truly equal.
And this matter applies specifically relative to the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum.
For in the levels after the tzimtzum,
since all the levels are in a manner of a chain of descent of cause and effect,
it is necessarily that the cause is above the effect.
And also relative to the light of the line,
the worlds have some relative value.
For since the coming into being of the worlds from the line is through the revelation of the line
(for every action is through the revelation of the actor),
necessarily they have some relative value relative to the line.
However, relative to the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum,
since from the perspective of the revelation of the light of Ein Sof it would be impossible for the worlds to come into being,
therefore it was necessary for there to be a withdrawal of the light, through which specifically a void and empty space was made for the existence of the worlds,
and therefore,
relative to the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum,
the worlds are utterly incomparable,
in a manner that Atzilus and Asiyah are truly equal.
And since the surrounding light that shines in the worlds in the manner of a makif, at least, is the revelation of the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum,
therefore,
through the surrounding light,
it is felt within them
(in the manner of a makif, at least)
that they are incomparable.
And this is that even in Atzilus and above Atzilus there is "above" and "below,"
for that they are in an order and gradation of cause and effect
(meaning they have relative value,
as above),
this is the "below" within them,
and that it is felt within them
(through the surrounding light)
that they are incomparable and as naught,
this is the "above" within them.
And likewise conversely,
that even in BYA there is the aspect of "above."
For the surrounding light,
encompasses and surrounds all the worlds,
even the worlds of BYA,
and therefore
(from the perspective of the surrounding light that exists within them in concealment and as a makif),
even in the creations there is ratzo and self-nullification,
which is the "above" within them.
And based on this, the doubled language of "above, above... and below, below..." will be understood,
for the "above" and "below" within the worlds are twofold.
First—that Atzilus is "above" and BYA is "below,"
and second—the self-nullification and ratzo
("above")
that exists even in BYA,
and the existence
("below")
that exists even in Atzilus and above Atzilus.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the light of the line has its root in two levels of the light before the tzimtzum—before and after the will arose—which are the roots of the surrounding light and the filling light.
section.t: And it is known
that the light of the line has a root also in the light before the tzimtzum.
For in the light before the tzimtzum there are
(in general)
two levels.
As it is before it arose in His will to emanate and create,
at which time it was above any connection to worlds,
and as it is after it arose in His will to emanate and create,
through which it became in the category of connection to worlds.
And these two levels are the root of the surrounding light and the filling light after the tzimtzum.
For the surrounding light, its root is in the light before the arising of the will,
and the filling light
(the light of the line)
its root is in the light of the arising of the will.
And this is the light of Ein Sof, ascending to the highest height without end and descending to the lowest depth without limit,
for these two aspects
(of "above, above..." and "below, below...")
are within the light of Ein Sof itself.
